Q: Remove confidence interval arrowheads in forestploter package A:

As @lailaps pointed out, the forest() function calls makeci_static() to draw the confidence intervals. makeci_static is not an exported function from the package. You can use ::: to see its source code, and find where it draws the arrowhead when CI is outside the plot limit:

getAnywhere("makeci_static")

# function(est, lower, upper, pch, size = 1, gp = gpar(), t_height = NULL, 
#          xlim = c(0, 1), nudge_y = 0) {
#  ...
#  lng <- linesGrob(x = x_pos, y = 0.5 + nudge_y,
#                   arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.05, "inches"), ends = arrow_side),
#                   gp = gp)
#  ...
# }

Apparently, the length of arrowhead is hard-coded to 0.05 inch and cannot be adjusted through other parameters. You can use body() to modify parts of the function and then assign the revised function back to the namespace of forestploter package.

temp <- forestploter:::makeci_static
body(temp)[[7]][[3]][[3]][[3]][[4]][[2]][[2]] <- 0
assignInNamespace("makeci_static", temp, ns = "forestploter")

After that, rerun your code and you will get the desired plot.

Q: How to auto approve renovate merge requests in gitlab? A:

Auto Approve Only

If you just want to enable automatic approval, then you need to do the following:

  • Set autoApprove to true in the renovate's global config (config.js):
...
autoApprove: true,
...
  • Make sure that the GitLab user for renovate has the right permissions (correct scopes) on its personal access token and correct role assigned (Developer atleast) to it on the group level or each repository level so it has the permission to approve the MR.
  • You need to make sure the following settings are disabled (unchecked) on the group level and repository level:
    • [ ] Prevent approval by merge request creator
    • [ ] Prevent approvals by users who add commits
    • [ ] Require user re-authentication (password or SAML) to approve

Both Auto Approve and Auto Merge

If you're interested in enabling both automatic approval and automatic merging, your renovate's global config (config.js) should look as follows:

...
autoApprove: true,
automerge: true,
automergeType: "pr",
automergeStrategy: "auto",
gitLabIgnoreApprovals: false,
platformAutomerge: true,
...

Also, check the rules under protected branches section to make sure it has the permissions to merge. You might have to change the role sometimes to Developer in case of merging if applying on group level.
